extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for Research Project Grants (R01/R03/R15/R21/R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating Research Project Grant applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), describing the standard review criteria, special-case considerations by mechanism, and additional review elements. Intended to be used when assigning overall impact and criterion scores and when preparing written critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R01, R03, R21, R34: likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the field(s). For R15: likelihood to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the research environment of the institution. Consider all review criteria and additional criteria as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Guidance — Small Research Grant (R03)
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail; reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Guidance — Academic Research Enhancement Award (R15)
rubrics_metrics.description: R15 objectives: (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 applications, but may be included if available. Reviewers should consider the R15-specific goals (strengthening research environment, exposing students) when assessing impact and other criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Guidance — Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant (R21)
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies with potential for significant impact. An R21 need not have extensive background or preliminary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should focus on conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to advance knowledge. Justification can be via literature, other-source data, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Guidance — NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant (R34)
rubrics_metrics.description: The R34 supports development of Phase III clinical trials — establishment of the research team, development of data management/oversight tools, recruitment strategies, protocol finalization, and operations/procedures manual preparation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R34 is not designed for collecting preliminary data or conducting pilot studies to support trial rationale. Reviewers should focus on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved? How will completion change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive this field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For R15 additionally: consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will substantially strengthen the school/academic component in terms of research environment and student exposure to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or early in independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects: assess complementary and integrated expertise, leadership approach, governance, and organizational structure. For R15: also assess suitable experience supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the concepts/approaches/instrumentation/interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether the application proposes a refinement, improvement, or new application of existing concepts/approaches/methods/instrumentation/interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the project is in early development, evaluate whether the strategy establishes feasibility and whether risky aspects will be managed. If involving human subjects/NIH-defined clinical research, evaluate plans for protection of human subjects from research risks and justification for inclusion/exclusion by sex/gender, race, ethnicity, and children, in terms of scientific goals and strategy. For R15 if clinical research: similar inclusion/protection considerations and whether application provides evidence the project can stimulate student interest in biomedical/behavioral careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess institutional support, equipment, and other physical resources' adequacy. Determine whether the project benefits from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements. For R15: also assess availability of well-qualified students and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving human subjects (non-exempt under 45 CFR Part 46), evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria: 1) risk to subjects, 2) adequacy of protection against risks, 3) potential benefits to subjects and others, 4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For research that meets criteria for exemption under 45 CFR Part 46, evaluate: 1) justification for the exemption, 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and 3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate proposed plans for the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, and inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if it is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate involvement of live vertebrate animals according to five points: 1) proposed use/species/strains/ages/sex/numbers; 2) justifications for use and appropriateness of species/numbers; 3) adequacy of veterinary care; 4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury (including analgesic/anesthetic/ tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices); and 5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for more details on evaluation of this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards exist, determine whether adequate protection (biosafety/biosecurity measures) is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether revisions address earlier concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate documented accomplishments, productivity, and whether the renewal justifies continued/expanded support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a specific line of investigation from the original application not recommended for approval previously, consider whether responses to prior comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider unique advantages conferred by foreign organization context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information in this section, including: 1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, 2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, 3) procedures to monitor possession/use/transfer of Select Agent(s), and 4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance and adequacy of proposed biosafety/biocontainment/security procedures for select agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable for: 1) Data Sharing Plan; 2) Sharing Model Organisms; and 3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reasonableness of plans to share data, model organisms, and genomic/GWAS data or the provided justification for not sharing. These comments inform program staff and may affect funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cost realism, appropriateness of requested resources/timeframe relative to aims and proposed activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to offer constructive suggestions, highlight major weaknesses, or advise on whether substantial revision is needed prior to resubmission.
